facts.fact: Banjul City Council market stalls are registered by QR code and market rates are collected digitally by market staff; three of the five pilot market zones had migrated to the new registration system by August 2022 and rate collection was reported up 25 per cent (UNDP Gambia).
facts.system: Banjul Smart Cities Pilot (QR stall registration and digitised market rate collection)

facts.fact: Only Banjul City Council, the capital, ran the Smart Cities Pilot, launched June 2022 in Albert Market; UNDP says it intends to scale some aspects to other councils in Greater Banjul.
facts.system: Banjul Smart Cities Pilot (QR stall registration and digitised market rate collection)

facts.fact: The pilot was set up by the UNDP Gambia Accelerator Lab with a local implementing firm and handed over to the council in June 2022; UNDP and the Singapore Centre for Technology, Innovation and Sustainable Development ran the initiative.
facts.system: Banjul Smart Cities Pilot (QR stall registration and digitised market rate collection)

systems.tiers: Banjul City Council, three of five pilot market zones
